title: Sprint bandwidth forecast and triggered decommitment rules
creator: Samantha Lee
description:
Problem: We lack an automated, repeatable way to detect when a planned sprint/cycle is likely to breach committed bandwidth and to trigger safe decommitment or scope-swap actions. This causes last-minute firefighting, missed OKRs, and opaque tradeoffs.

Objective: Design and implement a sprint-level bandwidth forecasting model and a set of triggered decommitment rules that: (1) forecast likelihood of breach 7 and 3 days before sprint boundaries, (2) propose minimal scope edits or staff role shifts, (3) surface deterministic actions in Console and Slack, and (4) provide manual overrides and audit logging.

Scope: MVP includes a conservative forecasting model using historical velocity, role-level focus factors, and open-ticket inflow; a rule engine to evaluate simple triggers (thresholds at 85% and 95% expected commit usage); UI signals in the Cycle Planner and a decommitment proposal email/Slack flow; a telemetry dashboard for simulations. Excluded: automatic reassigning of people without approval, automated cancellation of external commitments, and long-term capacity marketplace integration (future work).

Why now: High risk of scope slippage in enterprise onboarding cycles and Dedicated product work. Several recent cycles required emergency de-scoping with unclear criteria (see links). This feature will reduce manual coordination overhead and make scope tradeoffs auditable and repeatable.
acceptance_criteria: Forecasting job runs daily and produces 7-day and 3-day breach probability for every active sprint
Trigger rules produce a prioritized decommitment proposal (tickets to trim or swap) when expected bandwidth > 85% (warning) and > 95% (actionable)
Cycle Planner UI surfaces warning banners and a clickable proposal composer to submit decommitment changes
Proposal flow sends a Slack thread to the cycle lead with a one-click acknowledge and an option to escalate to EMs within 24 hours
Telemetry dashboard shows historical simulations for at least 6 prior cycles and includes a precision/recall summary for forecasted breaches
Runbook documented in Confluence with step-by-step manual override instructions and owners for on-call rotation
